title: bug: routeUnlandedLanding (finalize_attempt 'unlanded', and since task-efe07ce5 the finalizing close) moves a REVIEW row parked for a human (needsHumanReview) to WORKING with the flag still set, so a worker can claim a row the qa_reject hard cap reserved for a human
description: qa_reject has no finalizing fence and accepts any seat or a workerId-less human on the unassigned REVIEW row during a landing (qaReject.ts:137-155). A hard-cap reject there parks it REVIEW + needsHumanReview. If the landing then ends unlanded (finalize 'unlanded', or a deregister/DEAD-record close with no completion recorded), routeUnlandedLanding (state/workerLifecycle.ts) sends it to WORKING without checking needsHumanReview. claimNextTask.ts:574/636 fence only REVIEW+needsHumanReview, so a worker can then claim it. Likely fix: leave such a row in REVIEW (set landingRetry only, or plain close) inside routeUnlandedLanding, plus a test for each route.

finalizeAttempt.test.ts and state/finalizingCloseRetry.test.ts pass otherwise unchanged; docs/MCP_SERVER.md states the exception in moe.finalize_attempt and moe.deregister_worker.

implementationPlan.description:

- keep the status and the assignment: routing is {} exactly as for a non-REVIEW row, so it never goes to WORKING or BLOCKED and gets no blocked fields;
- STILL write landingRetry (count = prior + 1) and the one moe-daemon comment, with ', kept parked for human review (needsHumanReview)' appended. Then a human who later moves the row to WORKING hands the next worker a LANDING-RETRY with the rescue ref.
Update the function's docblock with one sentence for the exception. Leave every other path byte-identical: non-parked REVIEW to WORKING or BLOCKED (diverged, count >= 3), non-REVIEW unchanged, and retryUnrecordedLanding's guards. Both callers, finalizeAttempt.ts:153 and retryUnrecordedLanding, get the fix through this one function, so neither caller file changes. The prototype is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/7e735953-plan/proto-workerLifecycle.diff; apply it with your own Edit tool. Error handling is unchanged: it is a single updateTask write, and retryUnrecordedLanding's try/catch still keeps a failed write from failing the close.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: When a worktree landing ends unlanded, a REVIEW row that the qa_reject hard cap parked for a human (needsHumanReview true) stays REVIEW. It stays unassigned, keeps the flag and remains unclaimable by any worker or QA seat. This holds through both routes: finalize_attempt 'unlanded', and the finalizing close by deregister_worker, the DEAD-record prune or the startup purge. The landing-retry record and the moe-daemon comment are still written for whoever unparks it. Every other row routes exactly as today.
acceptanceCriteria: finalize_attempt 'unlanded' (conflict, and diverged) on a parked REVIEW row answers taskStatus 'REVIEW'. The task stays REVIEW, unassigned, with needsHumanReview true and reopenCount kept, and landingRetry.count is 1.
moe.deregister_worker, the DEAD-record prune and the startup purge each close the finalizing attempt and leave the parked row REVIEW, unassigned and flagged, with a 'contention' landingRetry.
After either route, a WORKING-pool or REVIEW-pool claim never returns the row, and an explicit-taskId claim is refused 'parked for human review'.
A REVIEW row without the flag still routes to WORKING, or BLOCKED on 'diverged' or the 3rd landing, and finalizeAttempt.test.ts and finalizingCloseRetry.test.ts pass unchanged.
invariants: A row with REVIEW + needsHumanReview is never moved by a landing outcome. Only a human path unparks it (release_task without a workerId, set_task_status, the board).
Non-parked routing (WORKING, BLOCKED for diverged or the 3rd landing, non-REVIEW unchanged) is byte-identical.
The diff is exactly workerLifecycle.ts, the new test file and the two MCP_SERVER.md sub-bullets.
compatibility: finalize_attempt's reply shape is unchanged. For a parked row, taskStatus reads 'REVIEW', and the wrappers never branch on it.
The LandingRetry shape and the comment format are unchanged apart from the appended parked note. Older rows and rows without the flag behave exactly as before.
